 Comment 2 1 3 React Share Lesia Tsurenko Announces Retirement at 37 and Shares a Heartfelt Farewell
 After 19 years on the professional tour, the former world No. 23 has decided to turn the page. In a lengthy message, the Ukrainian opened up about the struggles of recent seasons and her relationship with tennis.
 Lesia Tsurenko in Toronto in 2024. © AFP Jules Hypolite 16/11/2026, 15:42 2 min to read Follow us Tsurenko Lesia Tsurenko is calling it a career.
 At 37 years old, and after 19 years on the professional tour, the Ukrainian announced on Monday that she is retiring from tennis.
 Remove ads Ranked as high as world No. 23, a career-best she reached in February 2019, Tsurenko had not played on the tour since late 2024 and an appearance at the Billie Jean King Cup.
 "I didn't achieve everything I had hoped for"
 On her social media, Lesia Tsurenko posted a long statement explaining the reasons behind her decision:
 "I waited some time before being able to openly and sincerely thank tennis, because the past few years on the tour have left their mark and led me to doubt my love for this sport.
 But today, after taking a step back and doing some work on myself, I can say that I am deeply grateful for everything tennis has given me: all the opportunities, all the lessons, the moments of happiness and, of course, all the wonderful people I met along the way, who shared this experience with me and supported me throughout my career.
 [...] At the same time, I must acknowledge that I am going through a very difficult period. I didn't fulfill my childhood dreams and I didn't achieve everything I had hoped for."
 "My body often let me down"
 My body often let me down and, mentally, I didn't always manage to face the challenges that came my way.
 And I probably still need time to accept that things didn't unfold the way I had imagined when I was a little girl.
 But the most important thing I understand today is that a life without tennis is possible.
 It exists, and I can try to thrive in other areas. Before, I genuinely believed my life would end the moment my career did.
 [...] I realized that this world is far richer and more varied than I could have imagined. It offers so many opportunities, new challenges and, I hope, many more happy moments.
 I don't know what the next chapter of my life will look like, but for the first time in a long while, I'm curious to find out."
 Tsurenko had taken the WTA to court
 In 2025, Tsurenko underwent arm surgery, while simultaneously waging a legal battle against the WTA and its former CEO Steve Simon, whom she accused of psychological abuse in the context of the war in Ukraine.
 She did not win that case , having argued that the WTA, at the time, had an obligation to suspend Russian and Belarusian players from the tour.
 As for her record, Lesia Tsurenko won four titles on the main tour and reached the quarterfinals at the 2018 US Open, which remains her best Grand Slam result.
